To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

our SN rates are consistent with the current SN explosion models and with the star formation history of the Universe, that we find a correlation between SN rate and galaxy size, and that the SN rate in early-type galaxies is very low, indicating a low level of star formation in these galaxies.
the SN rate in the local Universe is 2.8 ± 0.4 SNe per century per L10 10 galaxy and 0.5 ± 0.2 per century per M10 10 galaxy.
the rates of core-collapse SNe and Type Ia SNEs increase with increasing galaxy mass, but the Type Ia SN rate is higher than the core-collapse SN rate in all galaxy mass ranges.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (1) how many SNe are produced by a galaxy of a given type and size, (2) how many of these SNe are detected by a given survey and (3) how do these rates depend on the properties of the galaxy.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Lick Observatory SN search has produced a large and homogeneous sample of nearby SNe and has laid the foundation for a reliable and accurate determination of the SN rates in the local Universe.
our control-time method is a powerful tool for calculating local SN rates, and the Lick SN rates are the most reliable and accurate rates to date.
the Lick sample is a well-defined sample with the best statistics and the most homogeneous observational data ever assembled for the study of local SN rates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have obtained a new set of SN rates for nearby galaxies.
the local SFR (star formation rate) has remained relatively constant for the past 10 Gyr, and the SN rate has remained constant for the last 2–3 Gyr.
we have developed a robust and efficient method to calculate the SN rates from a galaxy survey.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed rate of SNe is strongly affected by selection effects and the SN sample is not complete in the local Universe.
the SN rates derived from our data are robust, and they are consistent with the results from previous studies, which were derived from different samples and methods.
the local SN rates can be determined with a high level of precision.
